<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Pópulus Dómini, et oves páscuæ ejus: * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Pópulus Dómini, et oves páscuæ ejus: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Pópulus Dómini, et oves páscuæ ejus: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Pópulus Dómini, et oves páscuæ ejus: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Pópulus Dómini, et oves páscuæ ejus: * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Pópulus Dómini, et oves páscuæ ejus: * Veníte, adorémus.
b.6b7851c421:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> We are God's people and the sheep of His pasture, * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> We are God's people and the sheep of His pasture, * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> We are God's people and the sheep of His pasture, * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> We are God's people and the sheep of His pasture, * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> We are God's people and the sheep of His pasture, * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> We are God's people and the sheep of His pasture, * Come, let us adore Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Marcum
<r>Marc 6:47-56</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Cum sero esset, erat navis in médio mari, et Jesus solus in terra. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti venerábilis Bedæ Presbýteri
<r>Lib. 2, cap. 28 in cap. 6 Marci, tom. 4</r>
<c>L</c>abor discipulórum in remigándo, et contrárius eis ventus, labóres sanctæ Ecclésiæ varios desígnat: quæ inter undas sǽculi adversántis, et immundórum flatus spirítuum, ad quiétem pátriæ cæléstis, quasi ad fidam líttoris statiónem, perveníre conátur. Ubi bene dícitur, quia navis erat in médio mari, et ipse solus in terra: quia nonnúnquam Ecclésia tantis gentílium pressúris non solum afflícta, sed et fœdáta est, ut, si fíeri posset, Redémptor ipsíus eam prorsus deseruísse ad tempus viderétur.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Tentávit Dóminus Abraham, et dixit ad eum:
* Tolle fílium tuum, quem díligis, Isaac, et offer illum ibi in holocáustum super unum móntium, quem díxero tibi.
<r>℣.</r> Vocátus quoque a Dómino, respóndit, Adsum: et ait ei Dóminus.
<r>℟.</r> Tolle fílium tuum, quem díligis, Isaac, et offer illum ibi in holocáustum super unum móntium, quem díxero tibi.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to Mark
<r>Mark 6:47-56</r>
<c>I</c>n that time when it was late, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and Jesus himself alone on the land. And so on.

Homily by the Venerable Bede, Priest (at Jarrow) and Doctor of the Church
<r>Bk. ii, cap. 6, on Mark vi, 45</r>
<c>T</c>he toil of the disciples in rowing, and the wind contrary to them, is a figure of the diverse toils of the Holy Church, as, amid the waves of a world that fighteth against her, and the stormy blasts of unclean spirits, she laboureth to reach the rest of her Fatherland above, as a shore safe for her anchor. Here also it is well said that the ship was in the midst of the sea, and He alone on the land; for sometimes it cometh to pass that the Church is, by the great pressure of the Gentiles, not only so afflicted, but also befouled, that it seemeth as though, if it were possible, her Redeemer had for the time forsaken her.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The Lord did tempt Abraham, and said unto him:
* Take thy son Isaac whom thou lovest, and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.
<r>℣.</r> And when the Lord called him, he answered: Behold, here I am. And the Lord said unto him:
<r>℟.</r> Take thy son Isaac whom thou lovest, and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>U</c>nde est illa vox ejus inter undas procellásque tentatiónum irruéntium deprehénsæ, atque auxílium protectiónis illíus gemebúndo clamóre quæréntis: Ut quid, Dómine, recessísti longe, déspicis in opportunitátibus, in tribulatióne? Quæ páriter vocem inimíci persequéntibus expónit, in sequéntibus Psalmi subíciens: Dixit enim in corde suo: Oblítus est Deus, avértit fáciem suam, ne vídeat usque in finem.

<r>℣.</r> Cumque extendísset manum ut immoláret fílium, ecce Angelus Dómini de cælo clamávit, dicens.
<r>℟.</r> Ne exténdas manum tuam super púerum, eo quod tímeas Dóminum.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<c>W</c>hence it is that there cometh that cry of hers, when she is taken amid the waves, and the winds of temptations that break upon her, and with piteous entreaty she calleth on Him to protect her: Why standest Thou afar off, O Lord, why hidest Thou thyself in times of trouble? <n>Ps. ix. 22.</n> And then, in the verses that follow, she telleth Him what saith the enemy that persecuted her, saying: For he hath said in his heart God hath forgotten; He hideth His face, He will never see it. <n>32.</n>
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> The Angel of the Lord called unto Abraham and said:

<r>℣.</r> And Abraham stretched forth his hand to slay his son; and, behold, the Angel of the Lord called unto him out of heaven, and said:
<r>℟.</r> Lay not thy hand upon the lad; for now I know that thou fearest God.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>V</c>erum ille non oblivíscitur oratiónem páuperum, neque avértit fáciem suam a sperántibus in se: quin pótius et certántes cum hóstibus, ut vincant, ádjuvat, et victóres in ætérnum corónat. Unde hic quoque apérte dícitur, quia vidit eos laborántes in remigándo. Videt quippe Dóminus laborántes in mari, quamvis ipse pósitus in terra: quia etsi ad horam différre videátur auxílium tribulátis impéndere, nihilóminus eos, ne in tribulatiónibus defíciant, suæ respéctu pietátis corróborat.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Deus dómini mei Abraham, dírige viam meam:
* Ut cum salúte revértar in domum dómini mei.
<r>℣.</r> Obsecro, Dómine, fac misericórdiam cum servo tuo.
<r>℟.</r> Ut cum salúte revértar in domum dómini mei.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Ut cum salúte revértar in domum dómini mei.
b.e51be974df:

<r>Benediction.</r> May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>V</c>erily, He forgetteth not the prayer of the poor, neither turneth He His face away from any that putteth his trust in Him; yea, rather, to him whosoever is striving with the enemy, He giveth help to conquer, and, whosoever conquereth, to him He giveth an everlasting crown. For the which reason also it is here said plainly He saw them toiling in rowing. The Lord seeth them that are toiling in the sea, albeit He be Himself on the land. Although He seem for a moment to tarry in succouring the distressed, nevertheless the look of His love is strengthening them, all the while, lest they should faint and sometimes He setteth them free, even by an open deliverance, conquering all their adversaries for them, as when He walked upon the swelling of the waves, and stilled them.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> O God of my master Abraham, prosper my way which I go;
* That I may return again in safety unto the house of my master.
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, I pray thee, be merciful unto thy servant.
<r>℟.</r> That I may return again in safety unto the house of my master.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> That I may return again in safety unto the house of my master.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>

<c>C</c>onvertímini ad me in toto corde vestro, in jejúnio, et fletu, et planctu. Et scíndite corda vestra, et non vestiménta vestra, ait Dóminus omnípotens.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>E</c>cce jam noctis tenuátur umbra,
Lucis auróra rútilans corúscat:
Nísibus totis rogitémus omnes
Cunctipoténtem:

<h>U</h>t Deus nostri miserátus, omnem
Pellat languórem, tríbuat salútem,
Donet et nobis pietáte Patris
Regna polorum.

<h>P</h>ræstet hoc nobis Déitas beáta
Patris, ac Nati, paritérque Sancti
Spíritus, cujus réboat in omni
Glória mundo.

<r>℟.</r> Quia fuísti adjútor meus.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>L</c>o, the dim shadows of the night are waning;
Lightsome and blushing, dawn of day returneth;
Fervent in spirit, to the world’s Creator
Pray we devoutly:

<h>T</h>hat he may pity sinners in their sighing,
Banish all troubles, kindly health bestowing;
And may he grant us, of his countless blessings,
Peace that is endless.

<h>T</h>his be our portion, God forever blessed,
Father eternal, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Whose is the glory, which through all creation
Ever resoundeth.
Amen.

<r>℟.</r> Because thou hast been my helper.

b.0970247034:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>F</c>ebruary 14th 2027, the 8th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the Flaminian Way, the blessed martyr Valentine, a Priest, who after much healing and teaching was cudgelled and beheaded under Claudius Caesar, [in the year 268.]
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, the holy martyrs Vitalis, Felicula, and Zeno.
<h>A</h>t Teramo, [in Umbria, in the year 273,] the holy martyr Valentine, Bishop of that see. He was heavily flogged and committed to jail, but as he would not yield he was thrown out of the prison in the silence of midnight and beheaded by command of Placidus, Prefect of the city.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Alexandria, the Priest Cyrion, Bassian the Reader, Agatho the Exorcist, and Moses, who were all burnt with fire and passed away to heaven.
<h>A</h>t Teramo, [in the year 273,] the holy martyrs Proculus, Ephebus, and Apollonius, who were watching by the body of holy Valentine when they were apprehended by order of Leontius, the consular, and slain with the sword.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy martyrs Bassus, Anthony, and Protolicus, who were drowned in the sea.
<h>A</h>lso likewise at Alexandria, the holy martyrs Denis and Ammonius, who were beheaded.
<h>A</h>t Ravenna, the holy Confessor Eleuchadius, Bishop of that see.
<h>I</h>n Bithynia, [in the year 470,] the holy Abbot Auxentius.
<h>A</h>t Sorrento, the holy Abbot Antonino. He was in the monastery of Monte Cassino when it was destroyed by the Lombards, and he went thence to a solitude hard by the city of Sorrento, and there [in the year 830,] fell asleep in the Lord, famed for holiness. His body is daily remarkable for many miracles, most chiefly in the delivery of them that are vexed by evil spirits.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Ant.</r> Watch over us, * eternal Saviour, lest the cunning tempter seize us, for thou art made our everlasting helper.
<r>Canticle of Simeon</r>
<r>Luke 2:29-32</r>
§00.89b4b60b5f
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Watch over us, eternal Saviour, lest the cunning tempter seize us, for thou art made our everlasting helper.
b.6fe497a2e2:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>A</c>désto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: et concéde; ut hoc solémne jejúnium, quod animábus corporibúsque curándis salúbriter institútum est, devóto servítio celebrémus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.de6731704d:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>H</c>earken, O Lord, to our supplications; and grant that we may celebrate with devout service this solemn fast, which thou hast instituted for the healing of soul and body.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.2c19ba3169:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>A</c>désto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: et concéde; ut hoc solémne jejúnium, quod animábus corporibúsque curándis salúbriter institútum est, devóto servítio celebrémus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

<r>Commemoratio St. Catherine de Ricci, V., O.P.</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Veni, elécta mea, et ponam in te thronum meum; quia concupívit Rex spéciem tuam.

<r>℣.</r> Adducéntur Regi Vírgines post eam.
<r>℟.</r> Próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>I</c>ndulgéntiam nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, beáta N. Virgo et Martyr implóret: quæ tibi grata semper éxstitit, et mérito castitátis, et tuæ professióne virtútis.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.f88df543a7:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>H</c>earken, O Lord, to our supplications; and grant that we may celebrate with devout service this solemn fast, which thou hast instituted for the healing of soul and body.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of St. Catherine de Ricci, V., O.P.</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Come, O My chosen one, and I will establish My throne in thee, for the King hath greatly desired thy beauty.

<r>℣.</r> After her shall virgins be brought unto the King.
<r>℟.</r> Her fellows shall be brought unto thee.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we pray thee, that thy blessed handmaiden and witness N. in whom Thou hast ever been well pleased, because of her worthy maidenhood and her mighty showing-forth of thy power, may entreat thy pardon on our behalf.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.274e44e365:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Jube, domne, benedícere.
Reguláribus disciplínis instruat nos Magíster caléstis.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>D</c>onet Dóminus ut observétis hæc ómnia, tamquam spirituális pulchritúdinis amatóres; et bono Christi odóre de bona vestra conversatióne fragrántes: non sicut servi sub lege, sed sicut líberi sub grátia constitúti.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
Commemorátio Fratrum, Sorórum, Familiárium, Benefactórum defunctórum Ordinis nostri.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalmus 116</r>
§11.66d6af014b
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam.
<r>℟.</r> Et salutáre tuum da nobis.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>A</c>ctiónes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, aspirándo prǽveni et adiuvándo proséquere: ut cuncta nostra orátio et operátio a te semper incípiat, et per te cœpta finiátur.
Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Adjutórium nostrum ✠ in nómine Dómini.
<r>℟.</r> Qui fecit cælum et terram.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.71da482b7a:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
May the heavenly Master instruct us in the discipline of the Rule.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>M</c>ay the Lord grant that you observe all these things as lovers of spiritual beauty, and giving forth the good odour of Christ by your good life: not as servants under the law, but as free men established under grace.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
Commemoration of the deceased Brethren, Sisters, Relations and Benefactors of our Order.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalm 116</r>
§11.0a67a14e81
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Show us, O Lord, thy mercy.
<r>℟.</r> And grant us thy salvation.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>D</c>irect, we beseech thee, O Lord, our actions by thy holy inspiration, and carry them on by thy gracious assistance: that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and by thee be happily ended.
Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,
<r>℟.</r> Who made heaven and earth.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.ab491b8426:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.ddebf03d47:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
